classificationDefinitions.accepted-current: Only bytes present byte-identically on published master or explicitly admitted by a committed Integration acceptance record. No branch-only byte met this threshold in this audit.
classificationDefinitions.superseded-history: A later committed route, retirement, replacement, or archive record explicitly supersedes the earlier history.
classificationDefinitions.rejected-checkpoint: The commit or evidence explicitly records failed, rejected, or accepted=false state.
classificationDefinitions.evidence-only: Branch-only committed evidence, validation, handoff, or receipt bytes with no product admission; evidence status is preserved without turning it into acceptance.
classificationDefinitions.unresolved: Product/source/test bytes differ from master or status is not sufficient to determine admission; no disposition is guessed.

duplicateCherryPickedHistory.method: git cherry equivalence candidates only; not acceptance proof

steps: Freeze the published master commit and preserve every lane head as an immutable candidate reference.
Classify each lane path by exact blob and committed evidence status; admit only explicit Integration-accepted bytes.
Create fresh clean lane baselines from the accepted master tree, carrying unresolved commits as named review candidates rather than as implicit baseline ancestry.
Require a product-delta admission receipt before any unresolved source/test bytes become the next lane baseline.
rebaselineProposal.rollback: Discard only the proposed fresh lane baseline references; preserve all original branch commits and evidence unchanged.

limitations: No product source contents were opened; classifications use Git paths, blob identity, commit metadata, and committed evidence metadata only.
Git cherry-equivalence counts are ancestry/patch signals, not acceptance or duplicate-work proof.
Where no committed acceptance or rejection record exists, the inventory remains unresolved rather than guessing.
